title: Pairing new device dialog: Misleading message "Your Bluetooth adapter is not pairable." if one of two Bluetooth adapters are enabled
line: With two Bluetooth adapters and one turned off, the Add Bluetooth Device window no longer says the adapter is not pairable, and Make Pairable no longer turns the disabled adapter back on.
explanation: DiscoverPage::checkAdapters showed the 'not pairable' warning if any adapter was powered off or unpairable, even though the wizard only discovers with the usable (first powered) adapter. Its Make Pairable action then powered on and made pairable every adapter, re-enabling the one the user had turned off. The page now checks only the adapter it discovers with (warning when there is none but adapters exist), and Make Pairable only makes that adapter pairable, falling back to the old power-on-all behaviour when no adapter is powered.

commits.message:
wizard: only warn about the adapter used for discovery

The pairing page warned that the adapter was not pairable whenever any
adapter was off or unpairable, and Make Pairable powered all of them on.
Now it only checks and fixes the adapter it actually discovers with.

BUG: 489394

media.caption: Two adapters, hci1 turned off, hci0 working: the wizard warns 'not pairable' while already listing devices
Same setup with the fix: no warning, discovery on hci0 lists the device

reviews.text: Clean, minimal fix in bluedevil's DiscoverPage that aligns checkAdapters() and fixAdaptersError() with m_adapter (the usable adapter actually used for discovery). When one adapter is powered and pairable while another is turned off, the spurious warning disappears, and Make Pairable only modifies the active adapter unless no adapter is powered. Thoroughly verified with dbusmock across all multi-adapter states without breaking string freeze.

Correct root cause in bluedevil's DiscoverPage: the warning and Make Pairable now look only at m_adapter (the manager's usable adapter the page discovers with), so a deliberately disabled second adapter neither triggers the misleading message nor gets powered back on. The no-usable-adapter case keeps the old warning and power-on-all fallback, and adapterChanged/usableAdapterChanged still drive re-checks, so live changes are handled; the regression notes cover unpairable and powered-off hci0. Before/after screenshots match the reporter's scenario, and the commit message accurately describes the 14-line diff with no new strings. The reporter's idea of naming the adapter is a nice-to-have that becomes moot once the bogus warning is gone.
